source_text:
# A STRESS DOMAIN, NOT AN EXAMPLE — lives under qa/stress_domains/, not
# examples/, same reasoning waybill/ledger_ordering/nested_pieces already
# give in their own headers. Targeted at ANGLE-8: `authorize_scopes_or_
# refuses` (lib/hecks/fuzzing/properties/guards.rb:57-93) enforces
# `TenantScope.apply`'s tenant boundary, and that boundary exists ONLY
# for queries/read models — `authorize policy, tenant: field` is a word
# `QuerySpecification::Common::DSL` grants to `QueryBuilder`/`ReadModel
# Builder`, never to `CommandBuilder` (confirmed by reading the grammar
# directly: no `authorize` word exists on the command side at all). A
# WRITE that carries a `reference_to` from one tenant-scoped aggregate
# into another's is checked by NOTHING at dispatch time — `TenantScope`
# never runs for a command, and no `given`/`ensures` anywhere in this
# corpus checks a cross-aggregate tenant field either. `examples/banking/
# bluebook/safe_deposit_boxes.bluebook:261` (`authorize :vault_access,
# tenant: :branch_code`) is the ONLY `tenant:` declaration anywhere in
# the corpus before this domain — a single data point, on the READ side
# only.
#
# See this domain's own NOTES.md for what the first differential run
# found. `lib/hecks/fuzzing/properties/guards.rb`'s new `commands_
# respect_tenant_scope` (beside `authorize_scopes_or_refuses`) is the
# property this domain exists to feed.
Hecks.bluebook "TenantLedger" do
  vision "Two tenant-scoped aggregates, a cross-tenant reference_to between them, an entity, and a saga that crosses tenants — enough surface to prove the write side has no TenantScope equivalent at all."

  core

  # TENANT-SCOPED AGGREGATE ONE. `region` is this aggregate's OWN
  # declared tenant field — named the same way `authorize_scopes_or_
  # refuses` already reads a QUERY's tenant field (`declared.
  # authorization&.tenant`), just read here off `ByRegion` instead and
  # reused by `commands_respect_tenant_scope` as "the field that answers
  # which tenant this record belongs to," for ANY aggregate that
  # declares one, not only this one.
  aggregate "Ledger" do
    description "One region's ledger — the record a cross-tenant Transfer.Request can name without ever proving it belongs to the same region."

    identified_by :code

    attribute :code,          LedgerCode
    attribute :region,        LedgerRegion
    attribute :balance_cents, LedgerAmountCents, default: { value: 0 }
    attribute :entries,       list_of(Entry)

    value_object "LedgerCode" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a ledger is coded") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "LedgerRegion" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a ledger names its region") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "LedgerAmountCents" do
      attribute :value, Integer
      invariant("an amount is never negative") { value >= 0 }
    end

    value_object "EntrySequence" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("an entry is sequenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "EntryNote" do
      attribute :text, String
    end

    # THE PASS-THROUGH CORRELATION FIELD — carries `Transfer.Request`'s
    # own `reference` across the saga leg below so `SettleAcrossRegions`
    # can correlate `Transfer::TransferRequested` and `Ledger::
    # LedgerCredited` on the SAME scalar (`correlates_by :"reference.
    # value"`). NEVER stored on `Ledger` itself (no `sets` targets it) —
    # `CommandRules::Emission#emit` writes `payload: args` unconditionally
    # (every declared argument, not only `sets` targets), so a plain
    # declared attribute already reaches the emitted event without
    # needing a field to hold it. Its own type is a LOCAL value object,
    # not `Transfer`'s `TransferReference` — a value object is always
    # declared inside the aggregate that owns it (grammar-wide, checked:
    # no corpus site names one across an aggregate boundary), so this is
    # the same "same shape, redeclared, deliberately" move `SlipReference
    # `/`FolderReference` already make in ledger_ordering.
    value_object "LedgerCreditReference" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a credit still names the transfer that asked for it") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    # A PIECE ON ONE OF THE TWO AGGREGATES — the "an entity on one" half
    # of this domain's own construct list, same role `Visit` plays on
    # `SafeDepositBox`: nested state one level in, exercised by an
    # ordinary append (`Credit`, below) and its own command (`Annotate`).
    entity "Entry" do
      description "One posting into the ledger, in the order it landed."

      identified_by :sequence

      attribute :sequence, EntrySequence
      attribute :amount_cents, LedgerAmountCents
      attribute :note, EntryNote, optional: true

      command "Annotate" do
        role "Auditor"
        goal "Note something about a posting after the fact"

        attribute :note, EntryNote
        sets :note

        emits "EntryAnnotated"
      end
    end

    command "Open" do
      role "Clerk"
      goal "Start a ledger for one region"

      attribute :code,   LedgerCode
      attribute :region, LedgerRegion

      sets :code
      sets :region

      emits "LedgerOpened"
    end

    # THE SAGA'S OWN TARGET — dispatched by `SettleAcrossRegions` against
    # WHICHEVER ledger `Transfer.Request` named, cross-tenant or not.
    # Nothing here checks `region` against anything: no `given` reads the
    # dispatching Transfer's own region (a command cannot see the record
    # that triggered a saga leg — the saga's own memory is all a `dispatch
    # ..., with:` can pass in), and no runtime mechanism stops a saga from
    # crossing a tenant boundary a query would have refused outright. This
    # command is not a bug by itself — role "System" (an automated actor,
    # never a query's own caller) already reads as "not tenant-checked" the
    # same way every other cross-aggregate `dispatch` target in this corpus
    # (`Account::Debit`, `Account::Credit`) reads as "not customer-scoped."
    # The finding is that NOTHING ELSE in the whole dispatch closes the gap
    # this leaves open, and `commands_respect_tenant_scope` is what proves
    # that by checking the record this leaves behind.
    command "Credit" do
      role "System"
      goal "Credit funds into a ledger, settling a transfer that may or may not share this ledger's own region"

      reference_to Ledger
      attribute :amount_cents, LedgerAmountCents
      attribute :sequence,     EntrySequence
      attribute :reference,    LedgerCreditReference

      sets :balance_cents, increment: :amount_cents
      sets :entries, append: { sequence: :sequence, amount_cents: :amount_cents }

      emits "LedgerCredited"
    end

    query "ByRegion" do
      description "Ledgers open in one region, for a caller standing in that region."
      order_by :code
      authorize :ledger_access, tenant: :region
    end
  end

  # TENANT-SCOPED AGGREGATE TWO. Its OWN `region` is a plain, caller-
  # supplied argument at `Request` time — never derived from, or checked
  # against, the `ledger` it names below. That gap is the whole domain.
  aggregate "Transfer" do
    description "A request to move funds into some ledger — the ledger a caller names is never proven to share this transfer's own declared region."

    identified_by :reference

    attribute :reference,     TransferReference
    attribute :region,        TransferRegion
    # THE CROSS-TENANT reference_to — `Ledger` is a DIFFERENT tenant-
    # scoped aggregate than `Transfer` itself. Corpus precedent for a
    # PLAIN aggregate-level `reference_to` crossing between two
    # independently tenant-scoped heads: none before this domain — every
    # existing `reference_to`/`belongs_to` in the corpus (`SafeDepositBox
    # belongs_to Customer`, `Account reference_to Customer`) points at an
    # aggregate that declares no tenant boundary of its own at all.
    reference_to Ledger
    attribute :amount_cents,  TransferAmountCents

    value_object "TransferReference" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a transfer is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "TransferRegion" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a transfer names its own region") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "TransferAmountCents" do
      attribute :value, Integer
      invariant("an amount is never negative") { value >= 0 }
    end

    # THE WRITE-SIDE GAP, MADE CONCRETE. `sets :region` and `sets :ledger`
    # are both the BARE self-referential shorthand (`CommandBuilder#
    # resolve_bare_set!`) — importing `Transfer`'s own already-declared
    # `region`/`ledger` attributes verbatim, so a caller passes BOTH
    # directly: `region: "east"` and `ledger: "<any Ledger's own code>"`,
    # completely independently. Nothing here — no `given`, no runtime
    # check anywhere in `lib/hecks/runtime` — requires that the named
    # ledger's own `region` agree with the one declared right beside it.
    # `TenantScope.apply` (runtime/tenant_scope.rb) would refuse this in
    # a QUERY missing its `tenant:` arg; there is no equivalent refusal
    # for a COMMAND accepting one that disagrees with a cross-aggregate
    # reference. That silence is ANGLE-8's own premise, reached directly.
    command "Request" do
      role "Clerk"
      goal "Ask that funds move into a ledger, in a region the caller declares independently of which ledger they name"

      attribute :reference, TransferReference

      sets :reference
      sets :region
      sets :ledger
      sets :amount_cents

      emits "TransferRequested"
    end

    query "ByRegion" do
      description "Transfers requested from one region, for a caller standing in that region."
      order_by :reference
      authorize :transfer_access, tenant: :region
    end
  end

  # A PROCESS MANAGER WHOSE SAGA CROSSES TENANTS — `Transfer.Request`'s
  # own region and the `Ledger.Credit` leg's own target may belong to two
  # different regions, and the saga dispatches anyway: `SagaInterpreter#
  # deliver_saga_dispatch` (lib/hecks/runtime/saga_interpreter.rb) carries
  # no tenant concept at all, the same way `PolicyInterpreter#deliver`
  # doesn't either. One leg is enough to prove the saga machinery itself
  # adds no tenant check on top of what the aggregates already don't have.
  process_manager "SettleAcrossRegions" do
    correlates_by :"reference.value"
    starts_on Transfer::TransferRequested
    ends_on   Ledger::LedgerCredited

    transition Transfer::TransferRequested => "settling", from: "settling" do
      dispatch Ledger::Credit, with: { code: :ledger, amount_cents: :amount_cents,
                                       sequence: :reference, reference: :reference }
    end
  end
end
